result.title: Domain-Adapted Latent Diffusion Models for CT-to-PET Image Translation
result.summary: Positron Emission Tomography (PET) provides important metabolic information for tumor detection and staging but remains significantly less accessible than Computed Tomography (CT) due to its high cost, infrastructure requirements, and reliance on injected radioactive tracers. CT-to-PET image translation using generative models aims to address this disparity, yet state-of-the-art diffusion-based methods are limited by the scarcity of paired training data. To overcome this, we propose a domain-adapted latent diffusion framework that transfers natural-image priors using a relatively small dataset of 21,930 paired CT/PET slices, incorporating a signed power transform to resolve extreme intensity sparsity in PET data. Compared to CPDM, a state-ofthe-art baseline for CT-to-PET image translation, our approach yields superior performance in pixel-wise reconstruction and localized tumor fidelity, demonstrating effective transfer of natural-image priors to the medical domain. We further provide a systematic analysis of evaluation metric reliability for sparse PET data, showing that standard full-image metrics can be misleading indicators of translated image quality, and propose background-filtered and mask-restricted metrics as more clinically meaningful alternatives.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出面向 CT 到 PET 图像翻译的领域自适应 latent diffusion 框架，用约 2 万对切片迁移自然图像先验，并引入 signed power transform 处理 PET 强度极端稀疏问题，同时分析稀疏 PET 下评价指标的可靠性。
AI.relevance_reason: 属医学图像跨模态翻译与像素重建质量评价，不涉及 VLM 推理中的内部状态表示、证据筛选或停止决策，latent 在此仅指扩散模型的压缩空间；指标可靠性讨论虽涉及稀疏信号评估，但未给出可核查的 LVR 线索。
